question: v14
q: My power bill in Perth feels huge. Is that just me?

transcript.answer:
**Probably not a Perth-wide price jump.** The ABS CPI shows Perth electricity prices up only **2.4% year-on-year in August 2026**, the latest month available. Nationally, electricity prices were up **13.2%** over the same year, after rising about 22% in mid-2026.

Perth's price index has been nearly flat since March 2026 (0% or close to it each month, apart from a 2.4% rise in July). Most of the national increase happened in other states, so a bill that feels much bigger than last year is more likely due to something specific to your household:

- **Usage:** Hotter weather, more air-conditioning, a new appliance, or someone home more often can add a lot. Compare kWh used per day with the same quarter last year, not dollars.
- **Your plan:** A expired discount, a switch to a standard or default tariff, or a change to your supply charge or feed-in tariff can raise the bill even when unit rates barely move.
- **Government rebates:** WA's electricity rebates have been timed in ways that make the bill look different from one quarter to the next. Check whether a credit has ended or been applied late.
- **Billing period:** Some bills cover more days than others, so compare daily averages.

If you share the kWh used and the total for your last two bills, I can help you work out whether it's usage or price.
